title: Cross-Service Data Access
description: Learn patterns for accessing data across microservices without tight coupling.

data.text: Accessing data across services is one of the biggest challenges in microservices. Unlike a monolith where you can join tables across schemas, microservices require explicit APIs to share data. Netflix and Uber developed API composition and CQRS patterns to solve this.

data.title: Data Access Patterns
items: API composition: Gateway or BFF calls multiple services
CQRS: Separate read and write models, build denormalized views
Materialized views: Pre-combine data from multiple services
Change data capture: Stream changes to build synchronized views
GraphQL federation: Unified graph across multiple services

data.text: API composition is simple but requires multiple round-trips at query time. CQRS pre-builds denormalized read models, enabling fast queries at the cost of eventual consistency. Choose API composition for simple queries and CQRS for complex, high-traffic read scenarios.

data.title: The N+1 Problem
data.text: API composition can cause the N+1 problem. Fetching a list of orders with customer names requires 1 query for orders + N queries for customers. Use batching or GraphQL to solve this.

data.title: Example: CQRS for Order History
data.code: Build a denormalized order history view for the customer-facing UI.

# Write side: Order Service writes to Order DB
# Read side: Materialized view built from events

# Event: OrderCreated
# -> Update order_history table with customer_name, product_names, total

# Event: OrderShipped
# -> Update order_history set status = 'shipped'

# Customer UI queries order_history table directly:
# SELECT * FROM order_history WHERE customer_id = ?
# Single query, no joins, fast response

data.caption: CQRS read model flow
data.definition:
graph LR
    W[Write Model] -->|Events| E[Event Bus]
    E -->|Build| RM[Read Model]
    RM -->|Query| C[Client]
    C -->|Fast read| RM

items.question: When should I use CQRS?
items.answer: Use CQRS when you have complex read queries that require joining data from multiple services, or when read and write loads are very different.

items.question: What is GraphQL Federation?
items.answer: Apollo Federation lets you build a unified GraphQL schema from multiple services. Each service defines its own subgraph; the gateway composes them into a supergraph.

items.question: How do I handle cross-service transactions?
items.answer: Use the Saga pattern. Compensate for failures with compensating transactions rather than distributed ACID transactions.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: You cannot join data across services like in a monolith
API composition is simple but can cause N+1 problems
CQRS pre-builds denormalized views for fast reads
GraphQL Federation provides a unified data graph
data.takeaway: Choose the right pattern for your query complexity and performance requirements.
